recommendation:
NEWS. Use ESPN's two feeds as the whole basketball Wire for now: ESPN NBA (https://www.espn.com/espn/rss/nba/news) and ESPN WNBA (https://www.espn.com/espn/rss/wnba/news). Take the first item of each per day. Both feeds are in editorial order, so item one is ESPN's own top story. That gives one NBA item and one WNBA item a day from the same publisher under the same terms, which is the equal-coverage rule in its cleanest form. ESPN's RSS Terms explicitly allow display 'on a website or app'. The conditions: the headline stays verbatim (no ellipsis truncation, it wraps), the link is the feed's own URL, the text label says 'ESPN', no advertising goes near it, and the ARCHV note sits visibly apart as our words. The feeds carry no images, which suits the no-photos promise. Build a retry into the fetcher, because ESPN returned 202 with an empty body on the first request. Yahoo Sports (NBA and WNBA) is a fallback only. Its RSS clause allows display with conditions, but the same terms bar commercial exploitation without written permission. Most items come from other publishers (AP, USA TODAY, The Athletic, Pro Football Network, Gameday Chatter). The feed is newest-first rather than editorial. If used, filter to <source> = 'Yahoo Sports'. Dropped on the licence: CBS Sports, The Guardian, BBC Sport, CBC (the feed is also empty), Sportsnet, SB Nation/Swish Appeal, and NBA.com/WNBA.com (which have no feed). Worth one permission email each: The Next (theixsports.com/category/wnba/feed/, same-day, no terms page found) and Her Hoop Stats (Substack, weekly-ish). These are the independent women's-basketball voices that fit the brand. UK and Canada are uncovered: every UK and Canadian candidate is personal-use or needs a paid licence, so the basketball Wire is US-sourced only.

DATA. BALLDONTLIE is the one clean free source that covers the NBA and the WNBA equally. Commercial use and redistribution are allowed, no attribution is required, the free tier is 5 requests a minute, and a key is required, so the founder must register. The free tier gives teams and games (schedule and results) for both leagues but not standings: NBA standings sit on the $39.99/mo GOAT tier and WNBA standings on the $9.99/mo ALL-STAR tier. The recommended approach is to compute a daily record table (W-L, pct, games behind by conference) from final game results. Label it a record table, not official tiebreak order, and cross-check it against Wikipedia's CC BY-SA standings templates, which need attribution and share-alike. Avoid TheSportsDB free (tables empty, 1-5 events, and its terms bar App Store apps on the free key), ESPN's undocumented API (Disney terms are noncommercial), and NBA.com/cdn (403, and its terms bar commercial use and regularly updated stats databases, WNBA included).

WHAT EXISTS RIGHT NOW (26 Sep 2026). The WNBA regular season is over. TheSportsDB's last result is 25 Sep, Mercury 82, Aces 100, and ESPN's season metadata puts the regular-season end at 25 Sep. The playoffs start 27 Sep with four first-round games (Liberty at Lynx, Fever at Aces, Mystics at Dream, Wings at Valkyries). So the WNBA tab shows the final regular-season table plus playoff fixtures and results through October. ESPN's metadata puts the off-season from 1 Nov 2026 to 1 May 2027, when the table freezes. The first 2026-27 NBA fixture TheSportsDB lists is Raptors vs Heat on 3 Oct. The regular season starts late October, and the Wikipedia 2026-27 page has no standings section yet. Until then the NBA tab has fixtures only and an empty 0-0 table, and it needs a calm 'season starts' state. Uncovered: official standings with tiebreaks on a free tier, any non-US news source, and the WNBA's independent press until permission is granted.

Add a keyword filter for 'predictions', 'odds' and 'bet' to keep betting-adjacent items out. Everything else was dropped on its own terms: BBC Sport (business use needs a paid metadata licence), Sky Sports (personal non-commercial only, no automated collection), The Guardian (personal and non-commercial only; commercial Open Platform key needed), Autosport and Motorsport.com (personal use only), The Race (personal non-commercial only), formula1.com (RSS terms ban any commercial use and aggregation pages), RaceFans (reproduction prohibited), PlanetF1 (automated republication prohibited) and FOX Sports (non-commercial only). Getting to 2 to 4 sources needs written permission. In order of fit: FIA press office (neutral governing body; feed dates are clean; filter to 'F1' titles, drop transcripts), RaceFans (independent, calm tone, contact form offers licensing), BBC (metadata licence, may cost money), Guardian (commercial Open Platform key). Canada is uncovered: CBC has no F1 feed and requires a commercial licence, and Sportsnet has no F1 feed. DATA: the spec's host is wrong. api.jolpica.net does not resolve; the live host is api.jolpi.ca. Its endpoints return current standings, the next race (round 16, Bahrain GP in Malaysia, 4 Oct) and last results, with 4 req/s burst and 500 req/hour limits. But Jolpica's data is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, 'freely available for non-commercial use', and ARCHV is commercial, so email admin@jolpi.ca for written commercial permission before shipping it. OpenF1 is also non-commercial: avoid. The one source that allows commercial use without asking is the Wikipedia '2026 Formula One World Championship' article through the MediaWiki API (CC BY-SA 4.0, attribution and share-alike). It matched Jolpica exactly and was updated within an hour of the race, but it can be vandalised and is fragile to parse, so it needs sanity checks and a hold-yesterday fallback. Plan: ship the F1 tables from Wikipedia with a visible 'Source: Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0' line now, and switch to Jolpica if permission arrives. Neither ESPN nor any tested standings source gives an F1 thumbnail or logo that ARCHV would want, which suits the no-publisher-imagery rule. NEWS. Of 17 football publishers checked, only two have terms that allow a commercial third party to show a headline and a link.

1. ESPN soccer (https://www.espn.com/espn/rss/soccer/news). The RSS FAQ explicitly allows display 'on a website or app' if you show only feed content, keep the headline unchanged, link to espn.com and credit ESPN. That fits the Wire design exactly: verbatim headline, text label 'ESPN', no thumbnail (the feed has none) and no ads. One risk goes in the run report: Disney's master Terms of Use ban commercial use, and nothing reconciles the two documents. If the founder wants certainty, one email to ESPN would settle it.
2. The Conversation, English Premier League topic (https://theconversation.com/topics/english-premier-league-11809/articles.atom). CC BY-ND, with credit and link-back. About one item a month, so most days it is simply absent.

Dropped, with quotes above:
- BBC Sport: business use needs permission or a fee. Its Man Utd team feed is also just 4 podcast items.
- Sky Sports, The Guardian (RSS and the free API key), The Independent, The Athletic/NYT, manutd.com, Sportsnet/Rogers, CBS, FOX: all personal or non-commercial only. manutd.com even requires consent to link to it.
- CBC: non-private feed use needs an agreement, though a hand-placed hyperlink is allowed.
- Manchester Evening News and the Mirror: Reach geoblocks Canada, so the links would fail for ARCHV's own audience.
- TSN: no feed exists.
- talkSPORT and Yahoo: terms unclear.

So the aim of 2 to 4 permitted sources with a UK/US/Canada spread is not met. The only reliable daily football source is US-based ESPN. There is no permitted UK or Canadian source and no permitted Manchester United-specific feed. Two ways to close the gap are open to the founder, not to this run: (a) buy licences (BBC metadata licence, Guardian commercial key, or CBC's commercial RSS form); or (b) an editor-curated daily link, which CBC's terms expressly allow ('You may place links'). For Manchester United news, the Wire should rely on ESPN items that mention United, plus ARCHV's own Dispatch pieces.

DATA. Use football-data.org v4 on the free tier (registered key, 10 calls a minute, attribution line 'Football data provided by the Football-Data.org API'). The terms do not restrict commercial use. It covers the Premier League table and Manchester United's PL fixtures and results, and the Champions League if United are in it. Pull once or twice a day, never render the crest URLs it returns, and keep openfootball's CC0 JSON as a weekly-updated fallback and cross-check.

Not covered on free data:
- Manchester United's FA Cup, League Cup and Europa League matches: football-data.org paid tiers only.
- MLS table and fixtures: football-data.org 'Standard' tier at EUR 49 a month. Not in openfootball's JSON.
- Women's football tables (WSL/NWSL): none found free.
- UEFA Nations League and internationals: paid tier only.

TheSportsDB's free key is not allowed in App Store apps and returns only 5 table rows, so avoid it.

recommendation: NEWS: two feeds cleared the terms test for a daily Wire in golf, and both are American. (1) ESPN golf (https://www.espn.com/espn/rss/golf/news). Its own RSS Terms allow display 'on a website or app' as long as headlines, summaries and URLs are unchanged, there is no advertising, ESPN is credited and the item links to espn.com. The feed has no images. The items run in editorial order, so take the first item published in the last 24 hours that has not been used, not blindly item 1. (2) Yahoo Sports golf (https://sports.yahoo.com/golf/rss/). Yahoo's ToS RSS clause allows display without modification, with attribution and a link, and without ads. The feed is newest first and mostly partner content (Golfweek, Golf Channel, Golf.com, AP), so add a partner allow-list and dedupe, label items 'Yahoo Sports', and discard the content:encoded bodies. For both: keep the ARCHV one-line note visibly separate from the headline, keep shop or print promotions out of the Wire, and filter out betting titles ('odds', 'picks', 'bets'). No UK or Canadian golf feed cleared. BBC Sport requires permission for business use and may charge a fee. The Guardian, Sky Sports, Golf Monthly, National Club Golfer, CBC, Sportsnet, Golf Channel, NYT, CBS, PGA Tour and LPGA are personal or non-commercial only, or have no feed. Golf Canada and SCOREGolf (Canada) and Golf.com (US) are unclear. Golf.com's terms allow plain-text-named links but do not address headlines. These three are the best candidates for a short permission email; Golf Canada would give the Wire a Canadian voice and strong women's coverage. Women's golf: the official LPGA source has no feed and restrictive terms, so LPGA stories reach the Wire only through ESPN and Yahoo. On test day Yahoo's top item was an LPGA story. DATA: TheSportsDB is the one workable source. It covers PGA Tour (4425), European/DP World Tour (4426) and LPGA Tour (4553) equally, with schedules and a final top-10-plus-ties table (the 20 Sep BMW PGA result, JJ Spaun at -17, matched BBC). App use needs the $9/month Premium key, because the terms reserve app development for paid usage, plus a 'Data: TheSportsDB' credit and none of its artwork. Wikipedia's 2026 season pages (CC BY-SA, via the MediaWiki API) are the free cross-check for schedules and winners. The daily cadence suits both, since results post after final rounds. NOT COVERED: world rankings. OWGR allows only a logo-bearing Top-15 iframe widget and bans scraping. The Rolex Women's World Golf Rankings site could not be read and has no sanctioned feed. No clean source exists for either ranking, and to keep men's and women's golf equal, leave rankings out of the golf tab. Live leaderboards are out of scope by decision; ESPN's undocumented scoreboard API works but Disney's terms rule it out, and DataGolf is paid and betting-oriented.

recommendation: NEWS: two US sources pass. ESPN NFL RSS is the primary: the feed is fresh, and its order is editorial, so item[0] really is the top story. Its RSS page expressly allows showing it in a website or app, provided the headline and URL are left unmodified, ESPN is credited with a text label, and no ads appear. Two things to watch. pubDate is a batch stamp (9 of 22 items share one time) marked 'EST', so show the date or the first-seen time rather than trusting it. And ARCHV's one-line note has to be visibly ARCHV's own, not ESPN text. Yahoo Sports NFL RSS is the second, permitted-with-conditions under the RSS clause in Yahoo's ToS. It is mostly syndicated SB Nation and PFT copy in near-chronological order, so prefer the first item whose <source> is 'Yahoo Sports' (or label the partner), and throw away content:encoded, which carries full bodies and images. Everything else fails for a commercial publication. PFT/NBC, CBS, the Guardian and NFL.com are personal or non-commercial only; CBS and Fox are also betting-heavy. BBC needs a business permission or fee. CBC's feed is empty and marked personal use only. Sky Sports (UK), Sportsnet and the Globe (Canada) have no readable RSS grant; the NYT feed is dead. So no UK or Canadian NFL source clears the bar today. If a non-US voice matters, the licensed routes are a Guardian Commercial API key, BBC business RSS permission, or written OK from Sky or Rogers. DATA: nflverse-data 'schedules' games.csv (CC BY 4.0, no auth, updated automatically several times a day, tested fresh at 21:36 UTC today). Fetch it once a day for the week's fixtures and results, and compute a plain W-L-T table by division and conference; don't claim official seeding or tiebreakers. Credit 'nflverse' and drop the odds and spread columns at ingest. TheSportsDB's free key '123' works for eventsround, but it has no NFL table, next/past is capped at one event, and its terms bar App Store apps on the free tier, so it is a paid fallback at best. The spec's 'latestedges.php' path does not exist. ESPN's site.api and NFL.com are out on their terms. STILL UNCOVERED: a licensed UK or Canadian NFL news voice, official NFL standings with tiebreak seeding, and any logo-free 'next game' copy beyond what ARCHV derives from nflverse (which is enough for a daily, calm table). Research ran on Opus 5.5 (this agent); files are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-josephbankole-Claude-fifa-archv/102124d0-9054-4518-8f5d-f81d35074946/scratchpad/nfl/. The shared scratchpad root is being overwritten by parallel sport agents, so don't trust root-level feed files for NFL.

recommendation: NEWS: For a commercial app, only two tennis feeds have terms that actually permit showing a headline and link: ESPN (https://www.espn.com/espn/rss/tennis/news) and Yahoo Sports (https://sports.yahoo.com/tennis/rss/). Both are US. Use ESPN as the main tennis source. Its RSS page names "a website or app" outright, the feed carries no images, and the conditions are easy to meet: verbatim headline, the feed's own link, an 'ESPN' text label, no ads. Our one-line note has to sit visibly apart from the ESPN item. Yahoo can be the second source with lower confidence. Its RSS clause allows display without modification, but its general terms ban commercial reuse "unless otherwise expressly stated", and most items are third-party syndications (Tennishead, Tennis Gazette). The Wire should drop Yahoo if the founder wants zero ambiguity. Top-item rule: ESPN is editorially ordered, so take the first <item> dated in the last 24h. Yahoo is reverse-chronological, so take the newest non-duplicate. The UK and Canada are not covered. BBC needs a business licence, the Guardian's RSS and free API are non-commercial only (a paid Open Platform key would fix it), and CBC needs a signed agreement. Sky is unclear, since no RSS grant was found. Tennis Majors, Tennis365, NYT and CBS are non-commercial. ATP, WTA, Tennis.com and Tennis Canada have no usable feed. If regional spread matters, the cheapest fixes are a Guardian commercial key (UK) and a CBC agreement (Canada, strong on Fernandez and Auger-Aliassime). Ubitennis has no published terms and could simply be asked. DATA: No free API gives clean tennis rankings. The Wikipedia route is the only one that clears commercial use: the 'Current tennis rankings' page for ATP/WTA top-20 snapshots and the '2026 ATP Tour' / '2026 WTA Tour' schedules for 'next tournament this week' and last week's winners, all through the MediaWiki API under CC BY-SA 4.0 with attribution and share-alike on the derived tables. The data is editor-maintained. At fetch time the ranking tables said 'as of 14 Sep' while the ATP No. 1 legend said 21 Sep, so the component must display the as-of date and refuse to publish if it is stale or the parse returns fewer than 10 rows. TheSportsDB's free tier forbids App Store apps and has no tennis rankings or upcoming events. Wikidata ranking statements are too sparse. Paid APIs (api-tennis.com from $40/month) bundle odds and are not needed. Still uncovered: no live or daily match results beyond Wikipedia's winner cells, no doubles-focused or Canadian-specific data source, and no permitted UK or Canadian news feed without a licence.
